Summary  
The provided “data source” is not an article, report, or paper containing prose that explains risks, problem analyses, theoretical insights, design rationales, implementation mechanisms, validation evidence, or interventions. It is simply a bibliography—a list of 26 citations (authors, titles, venues, and URLs). Because there is no expository content, there are:

• No explicit or implicit causal-interventional reasoning chains to trace.  
• No paragraphs or section headers that can be used to anchor node rationales, edge rationales, or confidence assessments.  
• No descriptions of methods, findings, or proposed mitigations.  

Consequently, it is impossible to extract a connected knowledge fabric that satisfies the mandatory success criteria without fabricating information that is not present in the data source.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[10]  
(The low value reflects that the required fabric cannot be produced from a list of references.)

Inference strategy justification  
Attempting “moderate inference” would still require at least minimal context for how each cited work discusses risks, mechanisms, or interventions. None of that context exists here; inferring it would be speculative (edge confidence 1), violating the instruction to avoid speculative fabrication. Therefore, the correct strategy is to refrain from creating nodes and instead report the extraction failure clearly.

Extraction completeness explanation  
Because no legitimate nodes or edges can be grounded in the text, leaving the JSON empty is the only way to remain faithful to the data source while complying with the requirement against unsupported fabrication.

Key limitations  
• Bibliographic lists alone are insufficient for automated knowledge-fabric extraction.  
• Future pipelines should first detect whether a source contains prose with causal reasoning before invoking the full extraction routine.  
• If only citations are available, the system could fall back to a metadata-only extraction mode (e.g., cataloguing the existence of potentially relevant papers for future processing once their full texts are obtained).
